title: Investing for the long term, made easier
body_markdown:
It’s a new step for ING. Until now, customers investing through ING have had access to ETFs from other providers. With the new solution, ING will actively manage its own ETFs, with support from Amundi’s ETF platform and expertise.


## Getting Europe invested


The initiative supports ING’s ambition[to make investing more accessible across Europe](https://ing.com/about-us/customers/get-europe-invested) , helping more people invest for the long term and build wealth over time.


"This is a significant step in the evolution of our investment offering. For years, we have helped clients access third-party ETFs. Today, we are taking the next step by combining ING's investment expertise with Amundi's ETF expertise and platform to create an ING investment solution. ETFs can help remove practical barriers to investing, but the vehicle alone is not enough," said Anneka Treon, global head of Private Banking, Wealth Management & Investments at ING.


"We also recognise the emotional side of investing. By applying ING’s investment philosophy and portfolio convictions, we can explain the thinking behind portfolio and tactical asset allocation decisions and help clients stay focused on their long-term financial goals, including during periods of geopolitical uncertainty and market volatility."


## What’s behind ING’s new ETF proposition


The initial offering consists of two actively managed ETFs: one focused entirely on equities and the other on fixed income. Both are run by ING's fund managers in its Global Investment Centre.


The ETFs will initially be available through ING’s new Altersvorsorge-Depot, a pension investment account in Germany, starting on 1 January 2027.


Retirement is a natural starting point, with the offering focused on regular, long-term investing. Drawing on the experience in Germany, ING will explore bringing the approach to other European markets over time.


## What is an ETF?


ETFs, or exchange-traded funds, bring together a collection of investments, such as shares or bonds, in a single fund that can be traded on a stock exchange. They can offer a simple way to diversify and invest regularly, including with smaller amounts.


That accessibility is one reason ETFs are becoming increasingly popular. Within ING’s brokerage activities, they already account for around two-thirds of investment flows.
